title: Adaptive Honest Confidence Sets for Sparse Panel Interference via Loading-Subspace Decoding
banked_reason: terminal:laundering — the promised evaluable all-margin oracle frontier and adaptation ratio remain explicitly open; no bounded faithful field-tier repair exists.
gap_reasons: The proposal requires an evaluable, matching same-sample oracle frontier and adaptation ratio on every nonempty margin stratum, but this node expressly leaves the intermediate/disconnected-component profile open; its handle and modulus sandwich are not that deliverable.

The general oracle step is not established by the available modulus sandwich: upper and lower bounds evaluate sparse-compatible subspace moduli at different resolution constants, and that mismatch is material when a new loading component becomes statistically reachable.
No ratio formula is asserted on the unresolved intermediate-margin region.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a mathematically sound global adaptive expected-diameter frontier, weak-margin oracle equivalence, and a thresholded N=3, r=s=1 endpoint classification result; the math reviewer passed the claims actually proved. The load-bearing all-margin oracle characterization collapsed because disconnected loading components and finite classification transitions were left as an explicit open question, so neither an evaluable profile nor matching original-observation lower bounds were supplied for every nonempty margin stratum. A faithful completion would require a new component-aware finite decision program and matching minimax theorem, not a bounded repair of the existing derivation.
tldr: For the displayed nonempty Gaussian panel class with ordered loading and noise bounds and \(K\ge\sqrt r\), sparse direct and spillover effects are decoded from a post-period mean through a loading subspace learned from the untreated pre-panel. The proved results are a finite-sample globally honest confidence set with a sharp global-honesty expected-diameter frontier, equality of global and margin-oracle rates throughout the weak-margin region, and a maximal-margin adaptation gain in the \(N=3,r=s=1\) experiment once an explicit four-line classifier has error at most \(\alpha/2\). The same-sample oracle characterization over the remaining nonempty margin strata is not proved: disconnected loading components and finite classification transitions remain the central open question.
gap: HeLiShiMiao2026 turns panel interference into sparse robust regression but relies on a majority-valid-controls count, asymptotic selection, and coordinatewise inference. Sparse-confidence theory assumes an observed design, while projector-confidence theory does not propagate geometry into a causal sparse-vector diameter frontier. No opened paper characterizes global-versus-margin-oracle honest diameter when the loading operator is estimated from the same fixed-factor panel.
fill: The project combines an exact pre-panel second-moment region based only on the signal-versus-noise gap, finite support enumeration, every-sample diameter control, compensated-rotation lower bounds, and component-aware Gaussian decision inversion. On every nonempty primitive class it delivers the adaptive frontier, the weak-margin oracle equivalence, and a rank-one maximal-margin result from an explicit four-hypothesis experiment; the finite same-sample oracle profile on intermediate nonempty margins remains the open kernel.
